_comment: Registration for lib/project_next/collect.py (issue #1398, ADR 0008 census
row 23: `project-next.py` + the vendored engine, consumer `/project:next`,
class G - a gate that LETS WORK THROUGH, whose JSON output the command
document declares authoritative, so nothing downstream re-derives it).
WHAT THIS ASKS: a worktree whose `git status --short` call FAILS must be
reported UNEXAMINED (dirty=None), never read as clean. Before the fix,
`_parse_worktrees` turned the failure into `status = ""`, indistinguishable
from a worktree that was asked and found clean - and fed the cleanup
candidate text the LESS cautious, removal-leaning action instead of
"Inspect uncommitted changes; do not remove automatically".
WHY THE INVOCATION IS A CUSTOM SANDBOX, not a direct `{gate}` call: the
defect needs a REAL git-status failure (not a fixture that bypasses
collection), and the gate under test is one module inside a larger package
that scripts/project-next.py's CLI actually runs. Each case's `setup.sh`
(sourced, so its PATH export survives) builds a real git repository plus a
worktree whose own `.git` file is removed - a genuine, portable failure -
and arranges a fake `gh` shim so the CLI needs no network or token. The
invocation copies the CURRENT checkout (`git archive HEAD`) into a sandbox
and drops `{gate}` in as `lib/project_next/collect.py` before running the
real CLI against the fixture - so the anchor substitution (ADR 0008) swaps
in the OLD module while every other file (classify.py, rank.py, render.py,
scripts/project-next.py) stays current, exactly mirroring what changed.
DETECTION: the worktree's branch names issue #999, which the fake `gh
issue list` never returns - an unmapped, off-open-issue worktree, the
shape where `_dirty_worktrees_off_open_issues` (rank.py) and the cleanup-
action text diverge between `dirty=None` and `dirty=False`. `scripts/
project-next.py` exits 0 whenever the inventory is complete REGARDLESS of
classification, so `good_exit` alone cannot separate the two cases - the
invocation's own wrapper greps the rendered output for the status-unknown
phrase and translates its presence into exit 1 (absence stays exit 0),
which is what lets `detect_signal` and `good_exit` discriminate at all.
The unmapped worktree ALSO produces a `classification.unmapped_worktrees`
warning in both cases; that one is not the signal.
invocation: W=$(mktemp -d) || exit 9; git archive HEAD | (mkdir -p "$W/engine" && tar -x -C "$W/engine") || { rm -rf "$W"; exit 9; }; cp "$2" "$W/engine/lib/project_next/collect.py" || { rm -rf "$W"; exit 9; }; . "$1/setup.sh" "$W/fixture" || { rm -rf "$W"; exit 9; }; cd "$W/engine" || { rm -rf "$W"; exit 9; }; OUTPUT=$(python3 scripts/project-next.py "$W/fixture/repo" --full); pyrc=$?; echo "$OUTPUT"; rm -rf "$W"; [ "$pyrc" -ne 0 ] && exit "$pyrc"; echo "$OUTPUT" | grep -q 'status-unknown worktree .* names issue #999' && exit 1; exit 0
limits: Covers ONLY the git-status-collection path (_parse_worktrees). It says nothing about the other worktree_delivery re-read (#1257, which already defends in depth against this exact collector behaviour) or about a worktree whose `git log` call fails instead of `git status` - both commands share one try/except in the gate, so a case distinguishing them would need a different injection point than a real broken worktree supplies.

cases.name: bad-worktree-status-unreadable
cases.why: The worktree's own `.git` file is removed after `git worktree add`, so `git status --short` fails with a real, portable 'not a git repository' error - the gate must report this worktree UNEXAMINED, not clean.

cases.name: good-worktree-clean
cases.why: The identical unmapped-worktree shape with its `.git` intact - a genuinely clean, examinable worktree must still get the lighter cleanup action and no status-unknown warning.

anchors.why: The module as it stood immediately before #1398 - the commit the issue's own plan named as the anchor source. `status = ""` on a CollectionError, feeding `dirty=bool(tracked)` (False), is the exact behaviour under test; it MISSES the known-bad input (reports no status-unknown warning, and the lighter cleanup action) and AGREES with the current gate on the known-good one.
